subject: fishing spider
title: This Spider Catches Fish Up to Five Times Its Own Weight

scenes.text: A spider waits on the water. It isn't hunting flies.
Its back legs grip a rock or a plant. Its front legs rest on the surface.
When a fish brushes those legs, the spider grabs it and bites behind the head.
Neurotoxic venom stops the fish. Some catches weigh up to five times more than the spider.
It drags the fish onto land and melts it with digestive juices, feeding for hours.
Spiders like this fish on every continent except Antarctica.

description:
Some spiders catch fish, and a few have been seen taking fish up to about five times their own weight.
A 2014 review in PLOS ONE gathered fish-catching records from spiders on every continent except Antarctica: they anchor their back legs, rest their front legs on the water, bite the fish and drag it ashore to digest it.
Would you swim in a pond with these?
first_comment: Fish bodies in the records were on average 2.2 times longer than the spiders. Spider or fish: who are you rooting for?
